not_rules.note: Descriptive statement introducing the inverted pyramid concept.

anchor.quote: The basic structure of the inverted pyramid is:
The most important idea comes first or ‘above the fold’. This is the top part of a screen or a newspaper, where people can see the main idea at a glance.
This structure helps users scan content on any device. It also helps optimise the page for search engines.

not_rules.note: Benefits and rationale, not a text rule.

anchor.quote: An inverted pyramid is a structure for a piece of content: important detail comes first
Start with what the user most needs to know

not_rules.note: Heading grouping writing tips and steps (G-1).

anchor.quote: To structure your content as an inverted pyramid:

not_rules.note: Lead-in line to a list of writing guidelines.

anchor.quote: Write the main idea in as few words as possible. It can be a summary, a conclusion or recommendation, or the action someone needs to take.

not_rules.note: High-level editorial process advice / heuristic guidance (G-5).

anchor.quote: Describe the main ideas in headings.

not_rules.note: Duplicate of rules covered under headings guidelines (G-6).

anchor.quote: Under each of the top-level headings, group the content under subheadings. This helps people find supporting information.
Design pages based on how the user scans

not_rules.note: Heading introducing background on user reading behaviour (G-1).

anchor.quote: People start at the top of a page and decide within seconds whether to go past the initial view.

The headline and the first few lines provide the main reason for staying (or leaving). As people read through the content, they might also scan pictures or other headings, but they could also stop reading at any time.

The inverted pyramid works because people pay more attention when they first see the content. Their interest tends to wane in the middle, and sometimes they never reach the end. Journalists know that’s how readers behave and structure content accordingly.

rules.quote: Order the rest of the page from most to least important information.
rules.specification: Pages should present the most critical information first, followed by supporting details in decreasing order of importance.
rules.violation_condition: content ordered chronologically or with background information first rather than ordering from most to least important information
rules.why: G-1 and G-4: Consolidated general principle of inverted pyramid page structure into the primary instruction.

rules.quote: For long-form content, use a summary or a list of recommendations in the preliminary pages.
rules.violation_condition: long-form content that lacks an executive summary or list of recommendations in preliminary pages
when: Content is long-form content such as reports.
rules.why: Specific, actionable structural rule for long-form content.
